title: Emergency fund: how many months of expenses do you actually need?

audience.segment: adults with a regular paycheck and no savings cushion yet

learning_objective: After watching, the viewer can work out their own monthly essential expenses, pick a starter emergency fund target, and choose where to keep it.

key_points: A car repair bill arrives two days before payday: what happens next?
Without a cushion, surprise costs often land on a credit card
Who this is for: anyone without a few weeks of expenses set aside
Size the fund by essential expenses, not income
A common guideline is three to six months of essential expenses; your situation decides where you land
Illustrative household: essentials of 2,000 a month
Starter target 1,000, then one month, then three months
Round numbers for teaching only, not a recommendation
Counting money you plan to spend anyway
Keeping the fund somewhere it can lose value in a downturn
List last month's essential expenses and add them up
Set a starter target you can reach in about three months
Open or choose a separate, insured savings account and automate a small transfer on payday
Essentials, not income, set the size
Keep it separate, insured and easy to reach

short_form.concept: The essential expenses test: one quick way to find your emergency fund target
short_form.hook: Do you know how many months your savings would cover your essential expenses?

script_structure.notes: Open on the car repair bill and a calendar showing two days to payday.
What an emergency fund is for, and what it is not for.
Size it by essential expenses; present three to six months as a common guideline, not a rule.
Walk through the illustrative 2,000-a-month household with round numbers on screen.
Two mistakes, each with the fix.
Three steps the viewer can do this week.
Three-sentence summary and a pointer to the short.
Educational only, not personal financial advice. Check your own situation.

visual_direction.style: clean, calm motion graphics with a hand-labelled jar metaphor
motifs: a jar that fills month by month
data_visuals: bar showing 1, 3 and 6 months of the example household's essentials

sources: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (consumerfinance.gov): emergency savings guidance
FDIC (fdic.gov): deposit insurance basics for savings accounts

originality.notes: Original jar-and-calendar concept written for the pilot; no external scripts, visuals or branding used.
